# Germany Wants to Lead Autonomous Driving. Can It?

**From:** The AV Market Strategist <avmarketstrategist@substack.com>  
**Date:** 2026-11-25T06:31:35.000Z

---

View this post on the web at https://avmarketstrategist.substack.com/p/germany-wants-to-lead-autonomous

Waymo picked Munich, and Germany wants to become the lead market for autonomous driving. Yet five years after its Level 4 law, no driverless passenger service runs in regular operation.
Christian Hirte is Parliamentary State Secretary to the Federal Minister of Transport and one of the political faces of that goal. A lawyer and CDU member of the Bundestag, he previously served as the Federal Government Commissioner for Eastern Germany.
First, Munich. Christian explains what Waymo’s choice says about Germany’s legal framework, why foreign players are picking Germany now, how the KBA, the Bavarian authorities and the city of Munich share the approval work, and where the ministry stands on the rule changes industry and the KBA have proposed.
Then the industrial question. What is at stake for a car nation if value moves to software companies from elsewhere? Does it matter more that the driving software is European, or that fleets, depots and remote operations sit in Germany? And should Europe build a state-backed champion for autonomous driving, the way it built Airbus?
Finally, the road ahead. I ask what success as a lead market would look like, whether one federal authority should own approvals end to end, how rural areas and city outskirts get served when the business case is weak, whether public transport could order autonomous services like bus lines, and what Germany’s roads could look like in 2035.
